questions.question: The rate of a reaction doubles for each 10 K rise in temperature. By what factor does the rate increase when the temperature is raised from 298 K to 358 K? A 6, B 12, C 36, D 64.
steps: Temperature rise = 358 K - 298 K = 60 K
Number of 10 K steps = 60 / 10 = 6
Each 10 K step doubles the rate, so the factor = 2^6
2^6 = 64, so the answer is D

questions.question: A graph shows how the concentration of a reactant changes with time. Which expression gives the best estimate of the rate at time b?
steps: The rate at time b is the magnitude of the gradient of the tangent to the concentration-time curve at b.
The tangent drawn at b meets the concentration axis at about d and the time axis at about a.
Gradient = change in concentration / change in time = d / a (the rate is taken as positive), so the answer is B.

questions.question: Calcium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid. Which factor does not affect the rate? A concentration, B pressure, C surface area, D temperature.
steps: Concentration, surface area and temperature all change the rate of this reaction
Pressure only affects rate when gaseous reactants are involved
Calcium carbonate is a solid and hydrochloric acid is aqueous, so pressure has no effect
The answer is B

questions.question: A student wrote a mechanism for ethene reacting with chlorine to form 1,2-dichloroethane. Identify the two mistakes in the mechanism and give the correction for each.
questions.answer: Mistake 1: the curly arrow in step 1 starts at Cl and points to the C=C; it must start at the C=C double bond and point to the Cl delta+. Mistake 2: the carbocation is shown with delta+; it must carry a full + charge.
steps: Mistake 1: the first curly arrow is drawn from the Cl delta+ atom to the carbon. The electron pair of the C=C bond is what attacks the electrophile, so the arrow must start at the C=C bond and end at the Cl delta+ atom.
Mistake 2: the intermediate is a carbocation, which has a full positive charge (+) on the carbon, not a partial charge (delta+).
The other arrows are correct: the Cl-Cl bond breaks with the arrow from the bond to the Cl delta- atom, and the lone pair of Cl- attacks the C+ in step 2.

questions.question: Write the overall equation for Process A (ethene + chlorine, then cracking of 1,2-dichloroethane to chloroethene) and use it to calculate the percentage atom economy by mass for chloroethene.
questions.answer: C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl; atom economy = 62.5 / 99.0 x 100 = 63.1% (about 63%)
steps: Stage 1: C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H4Cl2 (addition)
Stage 2: C2H4Cl2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl (thermal cracking, elimination of HCl)
Overall: C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl; HCl is a by-product
Mr of desired product C2H3Cl = 2(12.0) + 3(1.0) + 35.5 = 62.5
Total Mr of reactants = 28.0 + 71.0 = 99.0

questions.question: Compare Process A with Process B (ethyne + hydrogen chloride, using toxic mercury(II) chloride catalyst that vaporises at the reaction temperature) in terms of atom economy and environmental impact. No calculation is needed.
questions.answer: Process A has the lower atom economy (about 63%, HCl is wasted) but a lower environmental impact; Process B has 100% atom economy but uses toxic, vaporising HgCl2 catalyst
steps: Process B is an addition reaction (HCCH + HCl -> CH2=CHCl), so all atoms end up in the product
Atom economy of Process B is 100%, higher than Process A (about 63%)
Process A produces HCl as a waste by-product, lowering its atom economy
Process B uses mercury(II) chloride, which is highly toxic and vaporises, so it has the greater environmental impact

questions.question: Explain the effects on the rate of increasing the temperature and of using a catalyst in a gas reaction, referring to a labelled Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution diagram.
questions.answer: Higher temperature: more particles have E >= Ea, more frequent and more energetic collisions. Catalyst: lower Ea, more particles have E >= Ea, so rate increases; the distribution itself is unchanged.
steps: Draw the curve with energy on the x-axis and number of molecules on the y-axis, with Ea marked
Higher temperature: the curve flattens and shifts right, so a larger fraction of molecules has E >= Ea
Higher temperature also gives more frequent and more energetic collisions, so more successful collisions per second
A catalyst provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy, shown by Ea moving left
More molecules now have E >= Ea, the area beyond Ea increases, so more successful collisions occur
The catalyst is unchanged at the end and the total number of molecules (area under curve) is the same, so the rate increases

questions.question: Sodium thiosulfate solution reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce solid sulfur. Which change would increase the time taken for sulfur to appear? A increase HCl concentration, B decrease thiosulfate concentration, C increase temperature, D add a catalyst.
questions.answer: B (decrease the concentration of sodium thiosulfate)
steps: Time for sulfur to appear is inversely proportional to the rate
Lower concentration of a reactant reduces collision frequency, so rate falls
Increasing HCl concentration, increasing temperature and adding a catalyst all increase the rate and shorten the time
So decreasing the thiosulfate concentration lengthens the time: answer B

questions.question: 0.100 mol of hydrochloric acid is added to 8.43 g of magnesium carbonate (Mr = 84.3). What is the total volume of carbon dioxide at r.t.p. (molar volume 24.0 dm3 per mol)? A 2.40 dm3, B 1.20 dm3, C 2400 dm3, D 1200 dm3.
steps: Moles of MgCO3 = 8.43 / 84.3 = 0.100 mol
Equation: MgCO3 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2O + CO2
0.100 mol HCl needs only 0.050 mol MgCO3, so HCl is the limiting reagent
Moles of CO2 = 0.100 / 2 = 0.050 mol
Volume = 0.050 x 24.0 = 1.20 dm3, answer B

questions.question: Which sketch graph shows the volume of carbon dioxide (y-axis) against time (x-axis) for the reaction in Q6?
questions.answer: B: a curve rising steeply at first, then levelling off
steps: CO2 is produced fastest at the start, when the acid concentration is highest, so the volume rises steeply.
The reaction slows as acid is used up, so the curve flattens.
It levels off at a constant total volume once the reaction is complete (the limiting reactant is used up): graph B.

questions.question: Which sketch graph shows the rate of reaction (y-axis) against time (x-axis) for the reaction in Q6?
questions.answer: A: a curve falling from a high initial value towards zero
steps: The rate is greatest at the start, when the concentration of acid is highest.
It falls as the acid is used up, because the gradient of the volume-time graph decreases.
It reaches zero when the reaction is finished: graph A.

questions.question: A reaction profile for a reversible reaction is shown. Which symbol represents the enthalpy change for R to P? Options: u, v, w, x.
steps: The enthalpy change for R -> P is the difference in energy between P and R.
In the profile, P is above R, and v is the arrow from the level of R up to the level of P.
u is the activation energy for R -> P and w is the activation energy for P -> R, so v is the enthalpy change (+ve, endothermic).

questions.question: Using the reaction profile for a reversible reaction, which symbol represents the activation energy of the reverse reaction P to R? Options: u, v, w, x.
steps: The activation energy of the reverse reaction P -> R is the energy needed to go from the level of P up to the top of the energy barrier.
This is the arrow w, from the level of P to the peak.
u is the activation energy of the forward reaction R -> P (from R to the peak).

questions.question: Using Hess's Law on the reaction profile in Q7, which expression is correct? A v+x=u+w, B w+x=u, C u-w=v, D u-v=x.
steps: Going from R to the peak is u (forward activation energy); coming down from the peak to P is w (reverse activation energy).
By Hess's Law the enthalpy change R -> P, v, equals the energy up to the peak minus the energy released coming down to P: v = u - w.
The other expressions do not hold: x points downwards (it is the enthalpy change of the reverse reaction, -v), so v + x = u + w and w + x = u are wrong, and u - v = w, not x.

questions.question: The energy profile for a reaction is shown. What is the minimum energy needed for the reaction to occur? Options: A X, B Y, C X-Y, D X+Y.
steps: The minimum energy needed for reactants to form products is the activation energy.
X is measured from the energy of the reactants up to the top of the barrier, so X is the activation energy.
Y is from the top of the barrier down to the products: the activation energy of the reverse reaction, which is not needed here.

questions.question: A graph shows how the concentration of iodine changes with time. What is the rate of reaction in mol dm-3 s-1 at 8 seconds? Options: A 0.01, B 0.02, C 0.03, D 0.25.
steps: The rate at 8 s is the gradient of the tangent to the [I2]-time curve at t = 8 s.
At 8 s the curve is at about 0.25 mol dm-3 and is flattening: it rises from about 0.23 at 6 s to about 0.265 at 10 s.
Gradient about (0.265 - 0.23) / (10 - 6) = 0.009, which is about 0.01 mol dm-3 s-1.
D (0.25) is the concentration at 8 s, not the rate.

questions.question: The Maxwell-Boltzmann curve for an uncatalysed reaction is shown with activation energy Ea. Which row shows the correct curve and activation energy for the reaction at a higher temperature with a catalyst?
questions.answer: C: curve Y with activation energy W
steps: A higher temperature moves the peak to a higher energy and lowers it, giving a flatter curve with more molecules at high energy: this is curve Y (X, with the higher peak further left, would be a lower temperature).
A catalyst provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy, so Ea moves to the left of the original Ea: this is W (Z is higher than Ea).
So the row is Y and W: C.

questions.question: Write the overall equation for the Liebig Process that makes potassium chlorate(V), KClO3. State symbols are not required.
steps: Add the two stages: 6Ca(OH)2 + 6Cl2 + Ca(ClO3)2 + 2KCl -> Ca(ClO3)2 + 5CaCl2 + 6H2O + 2KClO3 + CaCl2.
Ca(ClO3)2 is an intermediate that appears on both sides, so it cancels.
Combine the CaCl2: 5 + 1 = 6. The overall equation is 6Ca(OH)2 + 6Cl2 + 2KCl -> 2KClO3 + 6CaCl2 + 6H2O.

questions.question: Using your overall equation for the Liebig Process, calculate the overall atom economy by mass for the production of KClO3.
steps: Atom economy = (mass of desired product / total mass of reactants) x 100, using the overall equation.
Desired product: 2KClO3 = 2 x 122.6 = 245.2.

questions.question: Explain the type of reaction in Stage 1 of the Liebig Process, 6Ca(OH)2 + 6Cl2 -> Ca(ClO3)2 + 5CaCl2 + 6H2O, using oxidation numbers.
questions.answer: Disproportionation: chlorine (0) is oxidised to +5 in ClO3- and reduced to -1 in Cl- of CaCl2
steps: Oxidation number of Cl in Cl2 is 0
Cl in Ca(ClO3)2 (ClO3-) has oxidation number +5, so Cl is oxidised (loses 5 electrons per Cl)
Cl in CaCl2 has oxidation number -1, so Cl is reduced (gains 1 electron per Cl)
Ca, H and O keep the same oxidation numbers in every species
The same element is both oxidised and reduced, so this is a disproportionation (redox) reaction

questions.question: Describe a chemical test on a solution of the crystals to show the halide impurity is chloride rather than bromide, and give the expected results.
questions.answer: Acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous silver nitrate: chloride gives a white precipitate (bromide would give cream)
steps: Add dilute nitric acid to the solution to remove carbonate or other interfering ions
Add aqueous silver nitrate solution
Chloride ions form a white precipitate of silver chloride, AgCl
Bromide ions would form a cream precipitate of silver bromide, AgBr
A white precipitate confirms chloride impurity (optionally, it dissolves in dilute ammonia while cream AgBr does not)

questions.question: 1.52 g of impure KClO3 is heated until its mass is constant at 1.02 g. 2KClO3 -> 2KCl + 3O2, and the impurities do not decompose. Calculate the percentage purity, to an appropriate number of significant figures.
steps: Mass lost = mass of O2 released = 1.52 - 1.02 = 0.50 g
From 2KClO3 : 3O2, moles KClO3 = (2/3) x 0.0156 = 0.0104 mol
Limit to 2 s.f. because the mass loss (0.50 g) has 2 s.f.

questions.question: Give the systematic name of KClO4.
steps: KClO4 contains the chlorate ion with chlorine in oxidation state +7
Roman numeral (VII) shows the oxidation state of chlorine
Name: potassium chlorate(VII)

questions.question: A student investigated the role of the catalyst in the thermal decomposition of KClO3. Explain how each step of the procedure shows the catalyst is not used up.
questions.answer: Heating to constant mass completes the reaction; water dissolves the soluble KCl; filtering and rinsing leave the insoluble catalyst; drying removes water; the final mass is compared with the starting mass
steps: Step 1: heating until the mass is constant shows that all the KClO3 has decomposed, so only the catalyst and the soluble product KCl remain.
Step 2: adding water dissolves the soluble KCl but not the insoluble catalyst, so they can be separated.
Step 3: filtering collects the insoluble catalyst, and rinsing with deionised water washes off remaining KCl so that it does not add to the mass.
Step 4: drying removes water, which would add to the mass of the solid.
Step 5: weighing the dry solid and finding the same mass as the known starting mass shows the catalyst has not been used up.

questions.question: Using the diagram, explain how a catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction.
questions.answer: A catalyst provides an alternative route with lower activation energy, so more molecules have E >= Ea and the rate increases
steps: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy
On the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve, Ea moves to the left, so more molecules have energy >= Ea
More successful collisions occur per second, so the rate increases
The catalyst is regenerated and is not used up

questions.question: Which is the correctly labelled reaction profile for an exothermic reaction?
steps: In an exothermic reaction the products have lower enthalpy than the reactants, so the profile ends below where it starts.
The activation energy is measured from the level of the reactants up to the top of the peak, and the enthalpy change is measured from the reactants level down to the products level.
In A both are labelled correctly. B is exothermic but has the Ea and Delta H labels swapped. C and D show the products higher than the reactants (endothermic) and are mislabelled.

questions.question: The results of an experiment to determine the rate of magnesium with hydrochloric acid are shown. What is the approximate rate in cm3 s-1 at 40 seconds? A 0.75, B 1.3, C 2.2, D 6.0.
steps: The rate at 40 s is the gradient of the tangent to the volume-time curve at t = 40 s.
At 40 s the volume is about 89 cm3, and the curve is flattening, rising from about 81 cm3 at 30 s to about 94 cm3 at 50 s.
Gradient about (94 - 81) / 20 = 0.65 to 0.7 cm3 s-1, which is closest to 0.75.
B, C and D are too large: the rate is about 6 cm3 s-1 near the start but has fallen well below 1 cm3 s-1 by 40 s.

questions.question: Explain why calcium carbonate decomposes at a higher temperature than magnesium carbonate, in terms of the charge and size of the cations.
questions.answer: Ca2+ is larger than Mg2+ with the same charge, so it has lower charge density and polarises the carbonate ion less, so the carbonate is more stable
steps: Ca2+ and Mg2+ both have a 2+ charge
Ca2+ has a larger ionic radius than Mg2+, so its charge density is lower
A low charge density cation distorts (polarises) the carbonate ion less
Less distortion of the carbonate ion means the C-O bonds are less weakened, so more heat is needed to decompose it

questions.question: A gas syringe measures a maximum of 100 cm3 of CO2. Calculate the maximum volume of 0.500 mol dm-3 HCl that can be added to excess CaCO3 at r.t.p. without exceeding this volume. Molar volume = 24 000 cm3 mol-1.
steps: Moles of CO2 max = 100 / 24 000 = 4.17 x 10^-3 mol
CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O, so moles of HCl = 2 x 4.17 x 10^-3 = 8.33 x 10^-3 mol
Volume = moles / concentration = 8.33 x 10^-3 / 0.500 = 1.67 x 10^-2 dm3
Volume = 16.7 cm3

questions.question: Using the graph of gas volume against time for the CaCO3 and HCl experiment, calculate the initial rate of reaction, showing working on the graph and including units.
steps: The initial rate is the gradient of the tangent to the curve at t = 0.
Draw a tangent through the origin that follows the start of the curve; it reaches about 34 cm3 at 120 s.
Gradient = change in volume / change in time = 34 cm3 / 120 s = 0.28.
Units: cm3 s-1.

questions.question: The experiment is repeated with 0.250 mol dm-3 HCl, all else the same. State what happens to the initial rate and to the final volume of CO2 collected.
questions.answer: Initial rate decreases (about halves); final volume of CO2 decreases (about halves to about 45 cm3)
steps: A lower concentration of HCl means fewer particles per unit volume, so fewer collisions per second and a lower initial rate.
The graph levels at about 90 cm3, which is below the 100 cm3 the syringe could hold, so CaCO3 is in excess and the HCl is the limiting reactant.
Halving the concentration with the same volume halves the moles of HCl, so the final volume of CO2 halves to about 45 cm3.

questions.question: A catalyst increases the rate of decomposition of hydrogen peroxide by: A increasing the average kinetic energy of molecules, B decreasing the average kinetic energy, C increasing the activation energy, D decreasing the activation energy.
steps: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
It does not change the average kinetic energy of molecules, so A and B are wrong
Raising the activation energy would slow the reaction, so C is wrong
The answer is D

questions.question: A bottle of hydrogen peroxide is labelled 10 volume: 1 cm3 gives 10 cm3 of O2 at r.t.p. What is its concentration in mol dm-3? Molar volume = 24 000 cm3 mol-1. A 0.100, B 0.208, C 0.417, D 0.833.
steps: Moles of O2 from 10 cm3 = 10 / 24 000 = 4.17 x 10^-4 mol
From 2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2, moles H2O2 = 2 x 4.17 x 10^-4 = 8.33 x 10^-4 mol
This amount is in 1 cm3 = 0.001 dm3
Concentration = 8.33 x 10^-4 / 0.001 = 0.833 mol dm-3, answer D

questions.question: A Maxwell-Boltzmann curve for particles in a reaction mixture is shown. Which statement is correct? A position X is the mean energy, B Ea is the mean energy of particles that react, C the area under the curve to the right of Ea gives the number of particles with enough energy to react, D a catalyst moves Ea to the right.
steps: The area under the curve to the right of Ea is the fraction of particles with energy >= Ea
These particles have enough energy to react
Ea is not the mean energy, so A and B are wrong
A catalyst lowers Ea (moves it left), so D is wrong

questions.question: What happens to the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution when the temperature of the gas is decreased?
questions.answer: The peak moves to lower energy (left) and becomes higher and narrower; the total area stays the same
steps: Lower temperature means the average kinetic energy of molecules falls
The peak shifts to lower energy (left)
The curve becomes taller and narrower at the peak
The total area under the curve is unchanged because the number of molecules is the same, and fewer molecules now have E >= Ea

questions.question: The volume of O2 from hydrogen peroxide decomposition is plotted against time. What is the rate of formation of oxygen at point X? Options: A 1.3, B 2.5, C 4.4, D 25 cm3 min-1.
steps: The rate of formation of O2 at X is the gradient of the tangent to the curve at X (4 min, 17.5 cm3).
Reading the curve either side: about 15.8 cm3 at 3 min and about 18.7 cm3 at 5 min.
Gradient about (18.7 - 15.8) / 2 = 1.4, which is about 1.3 cm3 min-1.
2.5 is too steep for this late stage, 4.4 is the rate near the start, and 25 is the final volume.

questions.question: The time for iron(III) sulfate and sodium thiosulfate to react is measured with one drop of different solutions added. Which ion speeds up the reaction? A copper(II), B lead(II), C nitrate, D sulfate.
steps: With no added substance the reaction takes 205 s.
Only copper(II) sulfate reduces the time substantially (75 s), so a Cu2+ ion speeds up the reaction.
Sodium nitrate (204 s) and zinc sulfate (202 s) have no real effect, so nitrate and sulfate ions do not catalyse the reaction.
Lead(II) nitrate increases the time to 464 s, so lead(II) slows the reaction down.

questions.question: For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), dH = -192 kJ mol-1, what is the effect of a decrease in temperature? A rate increases and yield decreases, B rate increases and yield increases, C rate decreases and yield decreases, D rate decreases and yield increases.
steps: The forward reaction is exothermic (dH negative)
Lowering temperature shifts equilibrium to the exothermic side, so yield of SO3 increases
Lower temperature means lower average kinetic energy and fewer collisions with E >= Ea, so rate decreases
The answer is D

questions.question: For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), what is the effect of an increase in pressure? A rate increases and yield decreases, B rate increases and yield increases, C rate decreases and yield decreases, D rate decreases and yield increases.
steps: Pressure increases the concentration of gases, so rate increases
There are 3 mol of gas on the left and 2 mol on the right
Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles, which is the right
Yield of SO3 increases, so the answer is B

questions.question: 1.0 cm3 of 0.20 mol dm-3 K2CrO4 and 5.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 H2SO4 form an equilibrium. What is the effect on colour of adding 5.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 NaOH? A no change, B colourless, C more yellow, D more orange.
steps: Equilibrium: 2CrO4^2- (yellow) + 2H+ <=> Cr2O7^2- (orange) + H2O
NaOH reacts with H+ ions, removing them from the mixture
Lower H+ concentration shifts the equilibrium to the left (Le Chatelier)
More yellow chromate(VI) ions form, so the mixture becomes more yellow

questions.question: Why does the distribution of molecular energies start at the origin (0,0)? A some molecules have no energy, B all molecules possess some energy, C the temperature is 0 K, D some molecules do not have enough energy to react.
steps: The curve starts at zero because no molecule has zero kinetic energy
Every molecule has some energy, so the number of molecules at zero energy is zero
Option A is wrong, since the molecules are not without energy
The answer is B

questions.question: Some gas is removed from a sealed container, which is then cooled. How does the new distribution of molecular energies compare with the original?
questions.answer: The peak moves to lower energy and is higher and narrower, and the total area under the curve is smaller because there are fewer molecules
steps: Removing gas reduces the number of molecules, so the area under the curve falls
Cooling lowers the average molecular energy, so the peak shifts to the left
The curve becomes narrower and taller at the peak

questions.question: How does the peak of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution change when the temperature of the reaction mixture is decreased?
questions.answer: The peak moves to the left (lower energy) and becomes higher
steps: Lower temperature gives lower average kinetic energy
The peak therefore shifts to lower energy (left)
Because the total area is constant, the peak becomes higher and narrower

questions.question: The activation energy Ea of an uncatalysed reaction is shown on a Maxwell-Boltzmann curve with shaded areas A and B on either side of Ea. How do the two shaded areas change when a catalyst is added?
questions.answer: The area on the reacting side (energy above Ea) increases and the area on the other side decreases by the same amount; total area unchanged
steps: A catalyst lowers the activation energy, moving the Ea line to the left
More molecules now have energy above the new Ea, so the area on the reacting side increases
The same amount of area is lost from the non-reacting side
The total area under the curve stays the same because the number of molecules and temperature are unchanged

questions.question: Magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid. Which change would have no effect on the initial rate? A an increase in the volume of acid solution, B a decrease in temperature, C an increase in surface area of magnesium, D a decrease in concentration.
steps: Rate depends on concentration, temperature and surface area
Changing the volume of acid, with the same concentration, does not change the number of particles per unit volume
Decreasing temperature, increasing surface area and decreasing concentration all change the rate
The answer is A

questions.question: For Container 2, the temperature is increased. For which values would the energy value change? A Ea only, B Emode only, C Emode and Emean only, D Ea, Emode and Emean.
steps: Ea is set by the reaction, not the temperature, so it does not change
Raising the temperature increases the most probable energy and the mean energy
The answer is C

questions.question: For Container 3, at the same temperature as Container 1, the pressure is lower. For which values would the number of particles at that value change? A Ea only, B Emode only, C Emode and Emean only, D Ea, Emode and Emean.
steps: Lower pressure at constant temperature means fewer particles in the same volume
The whole Maxwell-Boltzmann curve scales down, so the number of particles at each energy value falls
This applies to Ea, Emode and Emean, so the answer is D

questions.question: For Container 4, at the same temperature and pressure as Container 1, the walls act as a catalyst. For which values would the energy value change? A Ea only, B Emode only, C Emode and Emean only, D Ea, Emode and Emean.
steps: A catalyst lowers the activation energy only
The temperature is unchanged, so Emode and Emean stay the same
The answer is A

questions.question: What happens to the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve when the temperature is increased? A peak higher and further right, B peak higher and further left, C peak lower and further right, D peak lower and further left.
questions.answer: C (peak lower and further to the right)
steps: Higher temperature gives higher average kinetic energy, so the peak moves to the right
The curve spreads out, so the peak becomes lower
The total area is constant, so a lower and wider curve results

questions.question: How does the diagram change if a catalyst is added? A Ea moves right and peak stays, B Ea moves left and peak moves right, C Ea moves left and peak stays, D Ea stays and peak moves right.
questions.answer: C (activation energy moves to the left and the peak stays the same)
steps: A catalyst lowers the activation energy, moving Ea to the left
The catalyst does not change the temperature, so the distribution curve and peak stay the same
The answer is C

questions.question: Which statement best explains why the rate of a reaction increases with temperature? A activation energy decreases, B number of collisions increases, C kinetic energy of particles increases, D frequency of collisions with E >= Ea increases.
questions.answer: D (frequency of collisions with E >= Ea increases)
steps: Activation energy does not change with temperature, so A is wrong
The number of collisions increases only slightly, so B is not the best explanation
The key effect is that more collisions have energy at least Ea
The answer is D

questions.question: An experiment measures the concentration of a reactant over time. What is the approximate initial rate? A 4.5 x 10^-5, B 1.8 x 10^-5, C 1.3 x 10^-5, D 2.0 x 10^-6.
steps: The initial rate is the magnitude of the gradient of the tangent to the curve at t = 0.
The curve starts at 0.0050 and the tangent at t = 0 reaches the time axis at about 105 s.
Gradient = 0.0050 / 105 = 4.8 x 10^-5 (a chord from 0 to 50 s gives a lower value, about 3.8 x 10^-5, because the curve flattens).
This is closest to 4.5 x 10^-5, which is option A.

questions.question: What are the units for the rate of reaction? A mol s-1, B mol dm-3 s-1, C mol dm3 s-1, D dm3 mol-1 s.
steps: Rate = change in concentration / time
Concentration is in mol dm-3 and time in s
Units = mol dm-3 s-1, answer B

questions.question: Magnesium ribbon (0.24 g) in 25 cm3 of 1.00 mol dm-3 sulfuric acid is compared with magnesium powder (0.24 g) in 50 cm3 of the same acid. What are the expected differences in observations in the second experiment?
questions.answer: C: the rate increases and the total volume of hydrogen is unchanged
steps: Magnesium powder has a larger surface area than ribbon, so the reaction is faster: the rate increases.
Moles of Mg = 0.24 / 24 = 0.010 mol. Moles of H2SO4 are 0.025 mol (25 cm3) and 0.050 mol (50 cm3), so the acid is in excess in both experiments.
Magnesium is the limiting reactant both times, so the same 0.010 mol of H2 forms and the total volume of hydrogen does not change.
So the answer is C (rate increases, total volume no change).

questions.question: Which change increases the proportion of particles that have sufficient energy to react? A increase reaction temperature, B decrease reaction temperature, C increase reactant concentration, D decrease reactant concentration.
steps: Proportion of particles with E >= Ea depends only on temperature (and catalyst)
Raising temperature shifts the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve right, increasing the proportion above Ea
Changing concentration alters the number of particles, not the proportion with enough energy
The answer is A

questions.question: Ethanedioic acid decolourises acidified potassium manganate(VII). Deduce the oxidation number changes for manganese and carbon.
questions.answer: Manganese from +7 to +2; carbon from +3 to +4
steps: In MnO4- manganese is +7, and in Mn2+ it is +2, so Mn is reduced
In ethanedioic acid, C is +3, and in CO2 it is +4, so C is oxidised

questions.question: Write the ionic half-equation for the reduction in this reaction with acidified manganate(VII).
steps: MnO4- is reduced from +7 to +2, gaining 5 electrons
Balance oxygen with 4H2O on the right and hydrogen with 8H+ on the left
Charge: -1 + 8 - 5 = +2, which matches Mn2+

questions.question: Write the ionic half-equation for the oxidation of ethanedioic acid in this reaction.
steps: Each carbon goes from +3 to +4, losing 1 electron each, so 2 electrons in total
Each ethanedioic acid gives 2 CO2
Charge and atoms balance with 2H+ and 2e- on the right

questions.question: Complete the table of rate indicator (1/t) for each volume of rhubarb juice used in the manganate(VII) experiment.
steps: The missing row is for 8 cm3 of rhubarb juice, with t = 261 s.
Multiply by 10^3 to give 3.83 s-1 in the last column.

questions.question: Plot a graph of the rate of reaction, (1/t) x 10^3, against the volume of rhubarb juice.
questions.answer: A smooth curve through the six points, rising steeply at first and levelling off near 4.1
steps: Label the x-axis "Volume of rhubarb juice / cm3" and the y-axis "(1/t) x 10^3 / s^-1", with scales that fill more than half of the grid.
Draw a smooth best-fit curve through them: the gradient decreases as the volume rises, and the curve levels off at about 4.1 by 9 to 10 cm3.
Do not join the points with straight line segments, and do not force the line through the origin.

questions.question: Explain why the rate of reaction is greater at higher concentrations.
questions.answer: More particles per unit volume give more frequent collisions per second, so more collisions have E >= Ea and the rate is higher
steps: At higher concentration there are more particles in the same volume
This increases the frequency of collisions per second
A greater proportion of these collisions have energy at least Ea, so more successful collisions occur

questions.question: Outline an experiment using the reaction between manganate(VII) and rhubarb juice to find the concentration of ethanedioic acid in the juice. Apparatus and calculations are not needed.
questions.answer: Titrate a known volume of acidified rhubarb juice with standard potassium manganate(VII) until the first permanent pale pink colour; use the 2:5 mole ratio
steps: Pipette a known volume of rhubarb juice into a flask and acidify with dilute sulfuric acid
Titrate with a standard solution of potassium manganate(VII) of known concentration from a burette
The end point is the first permanent pale pink colour (manganate(VII) is self-indicating)
Repeat for concordant titres and use the 2:5 mole ratio (MnO4- : H2C2O4) to find the concentration

questions.question: Draw a curve on the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution to represent the distribution at a higher temperature.
questions.answer: A curve from the origin with a lower peak further to the right, flatter overall, with a bigger area beyond Ea
steps: The new curve must start at the origin and never touch the x-axis at high energy.
Its peak is lower and at a higher energy (to the right of the original peak), so the curve is wider and flatter.
It lies above the original curve at high energies, so a greater area (more particles) lies to the right of the line at Ea.
The total area under the curve stays the same, because the number of particles is unchanged.

questions.question: Explain why increasing the temperature increases the rate of reaction.
questions.answer: Higher temperature increases the proportion of particles with E >= Ea and the frequency of collisions, so more successful collisions occur
steps: Higher temperature increases the average kinetic energy of particles
The Maxwell-Boltzmann curve shifts to the right and a larger proportion of particles has energy >= Ea
Collisions occur more frequently because particles move faster
More collisions have energy at least Ea, so more successful collisions occur per second and the rate increases
